title: What does 2400 square feet of land cost?
description: One acre of land costs fifteen lakh rupees, and the cost of two thousand four hundred square feet of the same land is found. One acre is forty three thousand five hundred sixty square feet, and the cost grows in the same ratio as the land, as in the conversion example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: a small plot is a small part of an acre, so its cost is the same part of the acre's cost. Watch for students who multiply the cost of an acre by the number of square feet directly.

video_script.why: The child scales a cost for one acre down to a small plot in square feet, using the same unit fact as the conversion example.
video_script.substitution: Write what one acre is in square feet, then match the ratio of cost to land for the small plot.
video_script.anchor: a land signboard reading one acre costs fifteen lakh rupees, with a small marked plot of two thousand four hundred square feet beside it
video_script.payoff_line: the plot costs about eighty two thousand six hundred forty five rupees

final_answer.spoken: eighty two thousand six hundred forty five rupees

maths_rules: 1 acre = 43560 square feet and costs 1500000 rupees
check: 2400 / 43560 is about 1/18 of an acre; 1500000 / 18 is about 83000, close to 82645
video_script.design: One idea: cost and land grow in the same ratio, so a small plot costs the same small part of an acre's cost. The signboard and plot stay in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.
open_questions: The book gives the cost as 1500000 rupees; the video says fifteen lakh rupees in Indian numbering.
